title: 2022 eruption of Hunga Tonga-Hunga Haapai
summary: On 15 January 2022 the undersea volcano Hunga Tonga-Hunga Haapai in the Kingdom of Tonga erupted violently. NASA analysis put the plume at 58 km, higher than Pinatubo’s 35 km. Tsunamis reached up to 65 feet above sea level on Tongan islands, destroyed hundreds of structures, displaced more than 1,500 people and killed four there, and struck Pacific shores, causing two deaths and an oil spill in Peru.

uncertainty.note: The eruption is dated 15 January 2022 by NOAA and NASA; USGS says it began at about 5 p.m. local time.

importance.justification: Plume reached the mesosphere (58 km) and tsunamis crossed the Pacific, per NASA and USGS.

beats.caption: The initial blast rose from the ocean surface to 58 km in about 30 minutes, reaching the mesosphere.
Tsunamis reached up to 65 feet above sea level on Tongan islands and struck shores around the Pacific.
More than 1,500 people were displaced and four died in Tonga, a low toll linked to daytime timing and tsunami awareness.

reviewer_note: Least sure: death toll varies by source (USGS and NOAA say four in Tonga; other offices differ), so only those two figures are used. Coordinates are the Wikidata location of the volcano. The NASA 58 km figure is a satellite estimate; the Pinatubo 35 km comparison is from the same NASA page.
